claims.claim: Restatements are written by the American Law Institute and are secondary authority.
claims.note: ALI describes Restatements as scholarly works written primarily for judges.

claims.claim: Court rules such as the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure are primary authority.
claims.note: Standard taxonomy; no page opened.

claims.claim: A decision from a higher court in the same system is mandatory; out-of-state decisions are persuasive at most.
claims.note: Standard doctrine; not checked against an opened page.

claims.claim: Erie Railroad Co. v. Tompkins (1938): a federal court in diversity applies state substantive law, including state common law as declared by its courts; no general federal common law.
Under the Supremacy Clause (Art. VI) valid federal law prevails over conflicting state law.
claims.note: Correct; no page opened.

claims.claim: A regulation that exceeds its authorizing statute is invalid.
claims.note: APA 706(2)(C): set aside agency action in excess of statutory authority.

claims.claim: The Caselaw Access Project was created by Harvard Law School Library from its printed reporters and made a very large body of U.S. case law public.
claims.note: Over 6.5 million decisions digitized 2013-2018; unrestricted release March 2024. Still available as open data (case.law); the original API/search service has been restructured, so describing it as a searchable site may be dated.

claims.claim: CourtListener is run by the nonprofit Free Law Project and offers opinions, oral argument audio and citation tools.
claims.note: FLP: 10M+ opinions, largest oral-argument collection, RECAP archive of PACER data.

claims.claim: govinfo is the GPO site; the eCFR is a continuously updated unofficial version; PACER charges per page with a waiver for small amounts.
claims.note: eCFR updated daily, unofficial editorial compilation. PACER $0.10/page, $3 cap per document; fees waived at $30 or less per quarter.

claims.claim: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (2024) overruled Chevron and requires courts to exercise independent judgment on statutory meaning.
claims.note: Decided June 28, 2024: "Chevron is overruled." Still current as of Oct 2026.

claims.claim: Prior decisions that relied on Chevron are not automatically invalid; their statutory holdings keep stare decisis effect.
claims.note: Court: mere reliance on Chevron is not a special justification for overruling such holdings.

claims.claim: Chevron U.S.A. v. NRDC was decided in 1984.
claims.note: Correct to my knowledge; no page opened.

claims.claim: A ruling on a motion to dismiss assumes the well-pleaded facts alleged are true.
Dicta are statements not necessary to the result and do not bind later courts.
claims.note: Standard definition; no page opened.

claims.claim: Disposition terms: affirmed, reversed, vacated, remanded.
claims.note: Standard; no page opened.

claims.claim: CREAC stands for Conclusion, Rule, Explanation, Application, Conclusion.
claims.note: Pedagogical convention; not checked.

claims.claim: IRAC stands for Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion.
claims.note: Not checked.

claims.claim: A promise to make a gift with nothing sought in return lacks consideration.
claims.note: Standard contract doctrine; not checked.

claims.claim: Church of the Holy Trinity v. United States (1892) held the alien contract-labor statute did not reach a church hiring a pastor from England, reasoning Congress aimed at manual labor.
After Loper Bright courts decide the best meaning of a statute themselves, giving agency views weight only for persuasiveness.
claims.note: Opinion requires independent judgment; agency views may inform (Skidmore-style respect).

claims.claim: Definitions of ejusdem generis, expressio unius and noscitur a sociis.
claims.note: Standard; no page opened.

claims.claim: A higher-court case in the jurisdiction controls and can only be distinguished, not disregarded.
claims.note: Not checked.

claims.claim: Rule synthesis combines several cases into one consistent statement of the rule.
claims.note: Pedagogical; not checked.

claims.claim: Mandatory adverse authority must be addressed.
claims.note: Model Rule 3.3(a)(2) requires disclosure of directly adverse controlling authority not disclosed by opposing counsel.

claims.claim: ABA Model Rule 1.1 requires competent representation (knowledge, skill, thoroughness, preparation).
claims.note: ABA site blocked (403); rule text not opened.

claims.claim: Objective memo parts: heading, question presented, brief answer, facts, discussion, conclusion.
claims.note: Pedagogical convention.

claims.claim: Work product protects material prepared in anticipation of litigation from discovery in many circumstances.
claims.note: FRCP 26(b)(3); not opened.

claims.claim: Twombly (2007) and Iqbal (2009): complaint must state a plausible claim; conclusory allegations are not entitled to the presumption of truth.
claims.note: Iqbal (2009) applies Twombly plausibility; Twombly LII page returned 404 so its year was not separately opened.

claims.claim: Rule 56: summary judgment if no genuine dispute as to any material fact and movant entitled to judgment as a matter of law.
Celotex v. Catrett (1986): party bearing the burden at trial must go beyond the pleadings with evidence.
FRAP 28 lists statement of issues, statement of the case, summary of argument, argument with standard of review, and a short conclusion stating relief sought.
FRCP 11: signer certifies after reasonable inquiry that legal contentions are warranted by existing law or a nonfrivolous argument for change, and factual contentions have evidentiary support.
claims.note: Rule 11(b)(3) also allows contentions identified as likely to have support after discovery.

claims.claim: On a motion to dismiss extra factual evidence is generally not considered.
claims.note: Rule 12(d): outside matters convert the motion to summary judgment.

claims.claim: Anderson v. City of Bessemer City (1985): clear error means a definite and firm conviction of mistake; no reversal merely because the court would have decided differently.
FRCP 52(a)(6) states the clear-error standard for findings of fact with due regard to credibility.
Ornelas v. United States (1996): reasonable suspicion and probable cause reviewed de novo; historical facts for clear error with due weight to local inferences.
The Bluebook is published by a consortium of law reviews; the Indigo Book is a free open alternative.
claims.note: Current Bluebook is the 22nd edition (May 2025), compiled by Columbia, Harvard, Penn and Yale law reviews; the 22nd ed. added a "contrast" signal the lesson does not mention.

claims.claim: The ALWD Guide to Legal Citation is a competing manual.
claims.note: Exists (8th ed. 2026 per search snippet) but no page opened.

claims.claim: Signal definitions: no signal = direct support; see = clear but indirect support; cf.; but see; contra.
claims.note: Not checked against an opened page; note Bluebook 22nd ed. added "contrast".

claims.claim: UCC Article 2 supplies gap-filling terms such as a reasonable price.
